title: Cisco XDR Open Incidents by Severity and Age
exclusions: Covers incidents in Cisco XDR only. Findings created directly in Enterprise Security or other tools need their own queue report.
evidence: Hourly report snapshots and the monthly count of incidents that breached their target, by severity.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Create a manual test incident in Cisco XDR with severity High and leave it unassigned. After the next input run it appears in `index=xdr` and the report lists it with `assignee=unassigned`; after 24 hours `breached` changes to yes.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Close the test incident in XDR. After the next input run its latest record has `status=Closed`, and it no longer appears in the report.

dataSources: `index=xdr sourcetype=cisco:xdr:incidents` from the Cisco Security Cloud (7404) XDR input, which polls `GET /iroh/private-intel/incident/search`. One JSON event per XDR incident with `id`, `title`, `status` (New, Open, Closed, Rejected, and containment states), `severity` (Critical, High, Medium, Low, Info, None, Unknown), `assignees{}`, `source`, and `incident_time.opened`.
app: Cisco Security Cloud (`CiscoSecurityCloud`, [Splunkbase 7404](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/7404)), Cisco XDR input.
spl:
index=xdr sourcetype="cisco:xdr:incidents" earliest=-30d
| dedup id
| where NOT status IN ("Closed", "Rejected")
| eval opened=strptime('incident_time.opened', "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S"), age_hours=round((now() - opened) / 3600, 1)
| eval assignee=coalesce(mvjoin('assignees{}', ", "), "unassigned")
| eval sla_hours=case(severity="Critical", 4, severity="High", 24, severity="Medium", 72, true(), 168), breached=if(age_hours > sla_hours, "yes", "no")
| table id title severity status assignee source age_hours sla_hours breached
| sort - breached, severity, - age_hours
description: Lists every Cisco XDR incident that is not closed or rejected, with its severity, status, assignee, source, and age in hours, and marks incidents older than a response target per severity (Critical 4 hours, High 24, Medium 72, others 168).
value: XDR correlates detections from Cisco and third-party products into incidents, but the SOC works its queue in Splunk. This report puts XDR's open incidents and their age next to the rest of the queue, so a critical XDR incident nobody picked up is visible in the same place as everything else.
implementation: Collect XDR incidents with the Cisco Security Cloud (7404) XDR input into `index=xdr`. Run the report hourly on a SOC dashboard and alert on unassigned Critical or High incidents past their target.
visualization: Table: id, title, severity, status, assignee, source, age_hours, sla_hours, breached. Supporting panels: open incidents by severity (single values), open incident age by severity (box plot or column chart).

references.title: Cisco Security Cloud App for Splunk User Guide
Cisco XDR Private Intelligence API: Incident

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Incidents worked in XDR** — analysts who work incidents in the XDR console may not update status promptly, so incidents look open longer than they are.

2. **Low-value sources** — some integrations create many Info or Low incidents. Filter by `source` if they flood the report.

**Suppression:** none for Critical and High; filter Info and None severities from the alert.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Cisco Security Cloud (`CiscoSecurityCloud`, Splunkbase 7404) on the search heads and on the heavy forwarder or Splunk Cloud Inputs Data Manager that runs its modular inputs.
• A Cisco XDR API client: in XDR under Administration > API Clients, create a client with read access to incidents and record the client ID and secret. Note the XDR region (North America, Europe, or Asia Pacific).
• Outbound HTTPS (TCP 443) from the input host to the XDR regional API host. The input requests an OAuth token with the client credentials; tokens are valid for 600 seconds and are renewed automatically.
• An index for XDR data (this page uses `index=xdr`) and a role with `srchIndexesAllowed` on it for the SOC.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
• In Cisco Security Cloud open Application Setup, choose the Cisco XDR card, and create an input with the region, the authentication method (client ID and secret), and the import time range. Set the index to `xdr`.
• The modular input calls `GET /iroh/private-intel/incident-summary/search` and `GET /iroh/private-intel/incident/search` and writes `sourcetype=cisco:xdr:incidents-summary` and `sourcetype=cisco:xdr:incidents`.
• The import time range sets how far back the first run reads; later runs pick up new and updated incidents. An incident that changes status is indexed again, so the search keeps the newest record per `id`.
• Check the fields this search needs: run `index=xdr sourcetype="cisco:xdr:incidents" | stats count by status severity` over 30 days.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=xdr sourcetype="cisco:xdr:incidents" earliest=-30d
| dedup id
| where NOT status IN ("Closed", "Rejected")
| eval opened=strptime('incident_time.opened', "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S"), age_hours=round((now() - opened) / 3600, 1)
| eval assignee=coalesce(mvjoin('assignees{}', ", "), "unassigned")
| eval sla_hours=case(severity="Critical", 4, severity="High", 24, severity="Medium", 72, true(), 168), breached=if(age_hours > sla_hours, "yes", "no")
| table id title severity status assignee source age_hours sla_hours breached
| sort - breached, severity, - age_hours
```

Understanding this SPL
• `dedup id` keeps the newest record for each incident, because updated incidents are indexed again.
• `incident_time.opened` is an ISO 8601 timestamp; `strptime` reads the date and time part, and `age_hours` is the time since it opened.
• The response targets in `case` are examples; set them to your SOC's agreed times.

Step 3 — Validate
• Compare with the Cisco XDR console Incidents page filtered to open statuses: the incident count and severities should match this report.
• Open one incident in XDR and confirm its title, assignee, and opened time match the row.
• Run `index=xdr sourcetype="cisco:xdr:incidents" | timechart span=1d dc(id)` over 30 days; days with zero events while XDR shows new incidents point to the input.

Step 4 — Operationalize
• Show the report on the SOC dashboard, refreshed hourly.
• Alert on rows with `breached=yes`, `assignee=unassigned`, and severity Critical or High, and throttle on `id` for 4 hours.
• Report monthly on breached incidents by severity and source.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting
• No cisco:xdr events and HTTP 401 in the input log: wrong client ID or secret, or the client was created in a different XDR region from the one selected.
• HTTP 403: the API client lacks read access to incidents.
• Events stop after a few minutes: the input host's clock is wrong, so the 600-second tokens expire early.
• Empty values in `age_hours`: `incident_time.opened` uses a different timestamp format in your data. Check one event and adjust the `strptime` format.
grandmaExplanation: Cisco XDR groups related security alarms into cases. We list the cases still open, how old they are, and which have waited too long for someone to handle them.
